DIAGNOSIS: Meige syndrome (idiopathic segmental cranial dystonia)

1. Tardive oromandibular dystonia with blepharospasm (often drug-induced, clinically identical presentation)
2. Secondary segmental cranial dystonia (e.g., due to a structural brainstem or basal ganglia lesion)
3. Hemifacial spasm (though typically strictly unilateral, it can occasionally present with bilateral or lower facial involvement)
